title: Reading Drill — Studying outdoor chess tables — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Studying outdoor chess tables — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The park recreation team had been asked to investigate pieces being moved by wind on exposed tables in Elmbrook. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on games interrupted by weather, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a three-week comparison, the team used player logs at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because different winds across the square might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward weighted pieces. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
